chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man, from Isma'il ibn al-Fadl,
who said: I asked Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) about the taqsir. He said: [It is obligatory] at four farsakhs.

key_terms.التَّقْصِيرِ: taqsir — the jurisprudential ruling obligating travellers to shorten four-rak'ah prayers (Dhuhr, 'Asr, 'Isha') to two rak'ahs once the qualifying travel distance is met
key_terms.فَرَاسِخَ: farsakhs — pl. of farsakh, a traditional unit of distance (~5.5–6 km); four farsakhs is the minimum one-way distance in Shia fiqh that triggers qasr prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum travel distance in farsakhs that makes shortening prayer (qasr/taqsir) obligatory according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: Isma'il ibn al-Fadl asks Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) about the minimum travel distance that triggers the obligatory shortening (qasr) of prayer. The Imam declares the threshold to be four farsakhs — a unit of approximately 5.5–6 km, placing the minimum qualifying journey at roughly 22–24 km. In the Shia legal tradition, this hadith is one of several transmitted in al-Istibsar that Shaykh al-Tusi reconciles with narrations specifying eight farsakhs (the two-way journey), explaining that four farsakhs is the one-way distance when travel is planned as a return trip on the same day.
